races.name: Betway Leigh Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f on Good ground and returns quickly on six days' rest for William Knight; Oisin Murphy's booking is a significant positive, and the hold-up style maps well to a race where a lone front-runner sets a controlled pace that a well-placed chaser can overhaul inside the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Mandarin Spirit
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides for in-form Kevin Ryan and this three-year-old's sole win came at 7f on Good, but placed form at 10f on Good suggests the trip is not a concern; a natural hold-up type who will race towards the rear and will need daylight to open up in the straight — 25 days off is manageable.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, which gives Colin Keane complete control of the early tempo; his best form is at 10f on Soft and this 12f trip on Good may test stamina limits, though the uncontested lead on a flat track could allow him to conserve energy and hold on for longer than his raw figures suggest.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's gelding has posted five consecutive placed efforts and clearly finds a way to be competitive, but his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed to midfield on the map — in practice he will race even further back than depicted, and Daniel Tudhope will need a wide, clean run in the straight to convert his consistency into victory.

runners_data.name: Claytons Kolatonic
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 59 and a significant 54-day absence for Dominic Ffrench Davis; a true hold-up horse bumped to midfield on the map, meaning the race shape works against him needing to find his natural position, and his recent form string of 63479 gives little encouragement at this level.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: Apprentice Molly Gunn (5lb claim) partners this lightly-weighted hold-up type for Lisa Williamson, whose yard has had no winners from four runners in the last 14 days; racing on 12 days' rest but the natural hold-up style is not accommodated by the map, and a rating of 52 makes this a tough ask in an open handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Relentless Hero is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and Colin Keane should be able to slot him straight to the front without a fight, dictating a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Haydock. With no genuine challenger for the lead, the early pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which means the race will compress into a tactical, turning contest where the winning move comes from those positioned to pounce off a steady tempo rather than grind one another down. Saxophonist, Claytons Kolatonic, and Lc Tiffen are all true hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are too many genuine closers for the race shape to accommodate them all at the rear — in practice they will race further back than the map shows, clustering behind the midfield pack rather than racing prominently. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a controlled pace with a field of closers strung behind — strongly favours a horse who can sit handy in second or third, travel within striking distance of the leader, and produce a sustained finish from off the pace; Brighton View and Mandarin Spirit, both comfortable hold-up types with proven form on Good ground, are best positioned to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Relentless Hero Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Relentless Hero bowls along uncontested at a sensible clip and the pack fails to coordinate a challenge early enough.
scenarios.body: Keane settles his horse into a rhythm with a field of closers strung out behind and simply dictates the pace of his own race, kicking at the two-furlong pole before the hold-up horses can organise themselves. The steady early tempo rewards a horse carrying the race forward who possesses enough stamina to hold on as the closers arrive late — Relentless Hero's recent 10f win on Soft suits the step up in trip here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that a well-placed hold-up horse cruising in second or third has the momentum to reel in and pass Relentless Hero inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Brighton View, winner over course-relevant distances on Good ground, is perfectly suited to a race where you stalk the lone leader and produce a clean finishing effort when the fractions are modest. Mandarin Spirit's previous win at 7f on Good and solid recent placed form at 10f means he has the turn of foot to capitalise if he travels powerfully into the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Catches All
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is deceptively fast enough to burn off the prominent pair and the genuine closers — despite their redistribution — produce strong late runs.
scenarios.body: Saxophonist, whose form shows consistent placing at 8-10f on Good ground, would benefit from a pace collapse that allows a true late burst to overhaul everyone, though his redistribution to midfield means he is not in his ideal position to maximise this. The scenario is constrained by the fact that all three redistributed hold-up horses (Saxophonist, Claytons Kolatonic, Lc Tiffen) are racing out of their natural position, reducing the probability that any of them delivers a clean finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position behind Relentless Hero causes interference or dramatic pace changes that scramble the expected running order entirely.
scenarios.body: An unsettled mid-race would most likely hurt the redistributed hold-up horses who cannot find clear daylight from the pack, while a horse that adapts quickly — such as Brighton View under the experienced Oisin Murphy — could find daylight at the right moment. Mandarin Spirit's previous exposure at this trip and on this going type gives him the composure to navigate a messy race better than lower-rated rivals.

watchPoints.text: Brighton View is on just six days' rest and returns with Oisin Murphy booked — watch for any market move at the off as that combination in a small field on Good ground can be decisive.
Relentless Hero's stamina at 12f on Good ground is unproven — if he shows signs of tying up after the two-furlong marker, the race could open up for the closers far more quickly than expected.

Saxophonist, Claytons Kolatonic, and Lc Tiffen are all genuine hold-up horses crammed into the midfield — watch for traffic problems in the straight if they become bunched behind Relentless Hero and cannot find gaps simultaneously.

The Good ground is consistent across all Haydock races today per the going report, so surface changes mid-card are unlikely to alter the tactical picture — horses with proven Good-ground form hold a reliable edge.

races.name: Betway Rose Of Lancaster Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Convergent
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's four-year-old has won twice at this trip on Good ground, and tracking Sallaal's controlled gallop from a prominent position is the obvious tactical play for Clifford Lee; the recent 1-4-5 form shows inconsistency but his two course-and-distance wins in similar conditions underline genuine claims here.

runners_data.name: Danger Bay
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's gelding has won three of his last seven on Good ground and is in excellent form at shorter trips, but in this five-runner field his natural desire to race prominently is compromised — Sallaal has prior claim on the front, meaning Tudhope is likely to find Danger Bay racing at a more restrained pace than ideal, which tempers his chance in this particular shape.

runners_data.name: Nahraan
runners_data.note: The Gosden-trained four-year-old brings strong form figures including three wins in five recent starts, and Murphy's quality is obvious, but his true style is prominent rather than the hold-up role his remapped position implies; 53 days off the track and the step up to 1m2f from his recent 10f runs add modest uncertainty, though his class is undeniable if Murphy can place him efficiently.

runners_data.name: Sallaal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's confirmed front-runner has won his last two starts at a mile and a quarter on Good and Soft, and Ray Dawson is well-placed to secure an uncontested lead in this small field; the hood is noted, and while his overall record is mixed at shorter trips, his stamina at this distance is proven and the lack of pace pressure is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: Sea Scout
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's gelding returns after a 287-day absence, which is the most pressing concern regardless of ability — his recent form of 3-3-4 at this trip on Soft and Heavy suggests he handles testing ground better than today's Good, and being a natural prominent type who cannot get his preferred early position in this field further dilutes his chance on return.

races.paceDynamic: Sallaal is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, Ray Dawson can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over Haydock's flat 1m2f on Good ground. Convergent is the most likely to press from a prominent position just off Sallaal's shoulder, while Danger Bay and Sea Scout — both natural prominently-ridden types — are likely to find themselves racing in a more restrained midfield role than suits them, simply because Sallaal has prior claim on the front. Nahraan, remapped to a hold-up slot, is not a natural closer and will be in a position that does not fully reflect how Oisin Murphy will want to ride him. This field holds more genuine prominent types than can all occupy that position at once: Sallaal is most likely to hold the rail lead comfortably, with Convergent best placed to capitalise on that real estate just behind. A controlled front-runner dictating an honest but not frantic tempo on Good ground at Haydock strongly favours a prominent racer who can track the pace and sustain a finish — Convergent's profile fits that shape most cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sallaal Controls, Pressers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sallaal leads at a measured pace and the race is decided in the final two furlongs by horses racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Sallaal sets a comfortable tempo from the front, and the race shapes as a test of sustained galloping ability rather than a sprint finish; horses who have tracked the pace are ideally placed to challenge. Convergent, proven at this trip on Good ground with a prominent style, is positioned to pick off the leader, while Sallaal's recent winning form over this trip gives it genuine claims to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sallaal Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that Sallaal's rivals leave him alone until too late and he simply outstays them.
scenarios.body: Dawson on Sallaal dictates entirely without pressure and the field never truly shortens the gap until the final furlong; by then, Sallaal's fitness edge and proven stamina at a mile and a quarter allow him to sustain the effort and hold on. His back-to-back wins and good-ground form at this trip underline that an uncontested lead is his most dangerous scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly dawdling and a bunched finish triggers a late sprint that suits a horse coming from an unexpected position.
scenarios.body: A very slow tempo could compress the field and allow Nahraan — though not a natural hold-up horse — to produce a late run from his remapped rearward position as the pace collapses and the field quickens simultaneously. This is a low-probability shape given the presence of a genuine front-runner in Sallaal who has little reason to go slowly, but Nahraan's class and Oisin Murphy's ability to find a run makes it conceivable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding or pace friction between the multiple prominent types scrambles the race shape and disrupts the fancied horses.
scenarios.body: Sea Scout and Danger Bay, both pushed back from their natural prominent berths, could cause interference or force rivals wide if they attempt to recover ground through the early stages; this chaos could allow a horse to steal a march. Sea Scout's absence of 287 days makes its contribution unpredictable, and any disruption narrows the field's collective advantage, handing a slim but real opportunity to the longest price.

watchPoints.text: Sallaal|Watch whether Ray Dawson can get Sallaal away cleanly and establish the lead without any early challenge from Convergent or Danger Bay, as any pressure in the first furlong would fundamentally alter the race shape and undermine the dominant scenario.

Sea Scout|After 287 days off the track, Sea Scout's early behaviour and jumping away from the gate should be monitored — any greenness or sluggishness on return could cause interference among the tightly grouped prominent types in this small field.

Nahraan|Oisin Murphy will need to decide quickly whether to push Nahraan forward from his remapped hold-up slot to recover his natural prominent position, and if he does, watch for crowding at the three-furlong mark where the course narrows and the field compresses.

Danger Bay|If Danger Bay is visibly restrained in the early stages against his inclination — which this pace map suggests is likely — watch his response at the two-furlong pole; horses racing below their natural rhythm often fire late but find the winner has already gone.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Dick Hern Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Alobayyah
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance last time and has a 2/5 record on similar going; William Haggas horse returns after 52 days but is a six-times winner over 8f on Good and is precisely the prominent stalker this race shape should suit — James Doyle-less here but Tom Marquand understands the role.

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: David Marnane's mare has a solid 9/15 record on Good going but her form is built racing prominently — in this 11-runner field with Silenciosa already at the head, she is unlikely to get her preferred position and will be forced to race further back than ideal, tempering confidence.

runners_data.name: Fallen Angel
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's Listed-class mare owns a remarkable 7W from 13 Good-going starts and has won this trip three times; returning after 86 days with a hood, she is the most credentialled prominent racer in the field and her pattern of tracking the pace then asserting is exactly what this scenario rewards.

runners_data.name: Maeva
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's hold-up filly returns after a lengthy 113-day break with a hood; all her best form has come on Soft or Standard, making this Good ground a genuine concern, and her record of just 0/8 wins/places on similar conditions is a significant flag.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's hold-up performer ran just 13 days ago and is proven on Good going with a win and multiple places; sits in the back-third naturally but will need the pace to be honest enough for his staying style to come into play over this trip.

runners_data.name: Noche Clasica
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this Edward Bethell hold-up type who has three wins on Good or Good-to-Soft ground over a mile; dropped out sharply last time (15th) but has previous form to suggest a recovery is possible if he gets a clean run through traffic.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old won last time and has a strong 5/7 record on Good going, but as a naturally prominent horse he is displaced into a midfield role by the race's structure — his chance is contingent on a clean passage rather than dictating his own pace as he prefers.

runners_data.name: Blingy's Sister
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old has good recent 8f Soft/Good form and Oisin Murphy takes the ride, which is an obvious positive; she is a true front-runner type who will not be able to express that in this field, and racing against her natural instincts in a midfield role makes her a harder proposition to assess.

runners_data.name: Calendar Girl
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's lightly-raced three-year-old returns after a remarkable 302-day absence having won three of four starts, all on Good or Good-to-Soft; the unknown fitness question after such a long layoff is the critical variable, but the talent and going profile are not in doubt.

runners_data.name: Pacific Mission
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's talented three-year-old has strong Going records on Firm/Good variants but all five recent efforts are placed or placed-adjacent rather than winning — a horse who runs well but tends to find one or two too good, and this Listed company could expose that pattern again.

runners_data.name: Silenciosa
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's three-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and Kieran Shoemark will have the luxury of an uncontested lead on Good ground; her two wins have come on Standard and Good-to-Soft, and her last Good-ground run (14th) is a slight concern, though the tempo control advantage is substantial.

races.paceDynamic: Silenciosa is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful pressure anticipated, Kieran Shoemark can dictate tempo from the front at a pace entirely of his choosing on Good ground over this flat Haydock mile. The prominent contingent — Fallen Angel, Alobayyah, Calendar Girl, and Pacific Mission — will fan out immediately behind her, likely forming a compact, organised chasing pack rather than a chaotic scramble, because the field's structure is defined by one leader and a cluster of genuine stalkers. Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice are all naturally prominent types who will be squeezed into a midfield role against their instincts, creating a muddled middle section that is unlikely to generate an effective late challenge from those positions. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner setting a fair but controlled pace — strongly favours horses who can track closely in second or third, stay on well through the final two furlongs, and quicken off a genuine tempo rather than a false or frenetic one; prominent stalkers with proven form on Good ground are the profile to concentrate on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silenciosa Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Silenciosa leads at a controlled but honest pace and the closest prominent trackers get a clean sightline from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Silenciosa sets a measured tempo, and those who track within two lengths — most likely Fallen Angel and Alobayyah — get the perfect tow into the straight and a fair test of quality; Good ground at Haydock rewards the horse who stays on most genuinely rather than the one who quickens from a standing start.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Silenciosa Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that Silenciosa simply never gets tired and the field fails to quicken past her in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to force the issue early, Shoemark dictates every fraction and then asks Silenciosa to stretch again in the final furlong when the field tries to come to her; a true front-runner's benefit of minimal energy expenditure in the middle mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the early-prominent horses are shuffled back, creating enough of a tempo for closers to thread through late.
scenarios.body: Noche Clasica or Mostar Dreams, sitting patient in the rear, would need a clear run through a compressed midfield group in the straight and enough pace to bring their staying ability into play; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected early clip that the sole front-runner is unlikely to set voluntarily.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramblers Collide
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, Aviatrice — contest for position early and disrupt the field's rhythm, producing a muddled race.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically fractious early phase would compress the field and create interference that benefits whoever lands the cleanest passage; Calendar Girl or Pacific Mission, with their tactical versatility, would most profit from the resulting chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Blingy's Sister, Rumba Numba, and Aviatrice all move for position immediately after the break — if they do, the early furlongs will be more scrambled than the pace map suggests and Silenciosa's uncontested lead assumption breaks down.

Calendar Girl returns from 302 days off; if she shows any sign of greenness or ring-rustiness in the paddock or the early furlongs, discount her chance significantly regardless of the talent on display.

Fallen Angel wore a hood today and returns after 86 days — watch the market and paddock behaviour closely; if she is fully tuned, she is the standout profile fit, but the layoff combined with headgear change warrants caution until the evidence is clear.

Maeva's 0/8 record on Good or faster ground is a structural concern in a race run on Good throughout — if the ground description firms up at all during the day, her chance recedes further from its already limited starting point.

Noche Clasica ran a deeply disappointing 15th last time on Good ground at this trip — if that run is excused by a specific issue (vet comment, traffic) watch for market confidence, otherwise the form evidence makes a straight reversal hard to justify.

races.name: Betway Ashton Heath Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: Two wins from five outings on Good ground at 7f underline strong course-condition fit; Tom Marquand takes the ride for the in-form Kubler yard (4 wins from 12 in 14 days), and this hold-up specialist wants a proper pace to chase — the uncontested Wechaad may not supply enough.|

runners_data.name: Pellitory
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a horse with a frustrating recent profile — four starts showing 2nd, 13th, 16th, 26th — suggesting the talent is there but consistency is elusive; O'Meara's 3/50 14-day strike rate is modest, and as a genuine hold-up runner Pellitory needs the race to be run at a pace that breaks the field apart.|

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old campaigned prominently who showed recent form of 1st over 8f Good and 2nd over 7f Soft; connections drop to McSweeney from a quieter yard (T14: 1/4), the 29-day absence is mild, and front-foot tactics give Yanifer the best chance of exploiting the straightforward pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Wechaad
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and holds the race by the scruff of the neck tactically; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that leading may not be his optimal mode, and his recent form of 4-7-3 at 7-8f on Good suggests competitive ability but no certainty once headed.|

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hannon and Levey combine with a horse whose natural inclination is to race from the rear — blinkers applied — but in a field with several hold-up types, Christian David is squeezed into midfield rather than his favoured last-to-first slot; last five runs show consistent placed form at 7-8f Good, so ability is not the concern, positioning is.|

runners_data.name: New Image
runners_data.note: The visor goes on for this David O'Meara runner who has won twice at 7f on Good but arrives just 7 days after his last outing and has shown 15th, 11th, 7th, 5th, 13th in recent form; a genuine hold-up horse in nature, running from a midfield map position dilutes his chance, and his recent consistency has been poor.|

runners_data.name: Moonshine
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3-year-old arrives after a 59-day break with Kieran Shoemark aboard and holds prominent-style form with two wins from six outings; the majority of those wins came at 6f on Standard, so stepping to 7f Good is a minor query, but front-end tactics in a controlled-pace scenario play directly to this profile.|

races.paceDynamic: Wechaad is the confirmed front-runner and, with no other natural pace horse to press him, is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good ground over this straight Haydock 7f. Moonshine and Yanifer will look to race prominently just off Wechaad's shoulder, creating a compact early order rather than a burning pace. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Christian David and New Image are genuine closers forced to track midfield in this race shape, meaning they are unlikely to get the true off-the-pace run that suits them best. A steady-to-fair pace set by a single front-runner on Good ground over 7f at Haydock typically rewards horses that travel prominently and quicken into the straight, making a prominent or pressing profile the clear tactical advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wechaad Leads, Prominents Win
scenarios.trigger: If Wechaad dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the race unfolds at a fair rather than searching tempo.
scenarios.body: Wechaad controls proceedings from the front and the energy cost is low enough that prominent pursuers Moonshine and Yanifer can close him down entering the final furlong; hold-up horses Christian David and New Image, racing out of their natural rear positions, lack the late sprint to pick them all off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true stamina test that benefits deep closers.
scenarios.body: A fast early tempo drains the leaders in the final 2f and allows the true hold-up runners Crimson Spirit and Pellitory to reel them in late; this scenario is tempered by the fact that Wechaad is uncontested and unlikely to force a genuinely searching pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Wechaad's uncontested lead develops into an unassailable advantage and the pack chases in vain.
scenarios.body: Without any rival willing to go with him early, Wechaad settles into a rhythm and conserves enough energy to repel all challengers deep into the 7f straight; this scenario is modestly discounted by the STYLE_FIT flag suggesting Wechaad is not entirely in his natural role here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the race degenerates into a sprint finish with no positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A false-pace affair would compress the field and make the outcome unpredictable, theoretically giving any runner a chance; however with Wechaad a confirmed pace-setter on Good going, a total pace collapse is unlikely and this scenario carries the lowest probability.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether anything challenges Wechaad early — if Moonshine or Yanifer push for the lead from the off, the pace intensifies sharply and the scenario shifts from controlled-front-runner to true-pace test, significantly altering which profiles benefit.

Christian David wears blinkers and Sean Levey may attempt to push forward from the gate to reclaim a more natural position — if that happens the declared pace shape is materially different and Wechaad's control is compromised.

New Image runs just 7 days after his last start with the visor fitted for the first time; monitor in the pre-race market and paddock for signs that the quick turnaround has not left a flat horse — a lifeless show would depress the entire hold-up scenario.

Crimson Spirit's trainer Kubler is running at a 33% 14-day strike rate (4/12) which stands out in this field; if market support appears pre-race it warrants attention given the form record on exactly this trip and going combination.

Moonshine's 59-day absence is the longest in the field — Ed Walker runners return fresh but the step from 6f wins on Standard to 7f Good is an untested combination for this horse, and a slow early show out of the stalls would undermine a prominent-position strategy entirely.

races.name: Betway Tanners Bridge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Galba
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Kevin & Lauren Frost who has placed three times on good ground but is still seeking a win; Conor Whiteley's claim helps the weight, and 10 days since last run looks fine — needs the pace to truly collapse late.|

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: In excellent form with two wins from last four on good ground, and Liam Wright's 5lb claim is significant; strong record at this distance on this surface and the hold-up style is tailor-made for the pace scenario this race will generate.|

runners_data.name: Comprador
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners and will press hard from the start alongside Napolian; has been consistent in placing but yet to win in six career starts, and the 49-day absence following a disappointing last outing is a question mark under Clifford Lee.|

runners_data.name: Black Endeavour
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from nine runs on good ground; stepping up to 7f for just the second time after winning at 6f, and the hood (first-time tongue tie) is worth monitoring — Kieran Shoemark in the saddle adds confidence for this longer test.|

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by David O'Meara who won most recently over 8f on good ground, suggesting stamina is not the issue here — the concern is whether he can dominate early when Comprador and Horace Wallace are equally committed to the lead.|

runners_data.name: Crafty Blue
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's runner has won twice and is rated on a going preference for good/standard, but his true style is a hold-up closer — placed in midfield on the map because the race lacks room for all natural rear-dwellers, meaning he is likely to race out of his ideal role and that tempers his chance markedly.|

runners_data.name: Flyta
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fine record at this distance on good ground (two wins from eight runs); Jack Mitchell rides for Mark Loughnane and the horse's consistent placed form over 7-8f on good suggests it will travel well and finish strongly if the pace is genuine.|

runners_data.name: Berlinetta
runners_data.note: Won last time on good ground over 8f, so stamina at 7f is clearly fine; George Bass rides for Jack Channon from a prominent position and the recent win plus solid placings on good ground make this horse a credible each-way player in the tracking role.|

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's mount has placed five times in ten starts on good ground without winning, and while he is a natural hold-up type, the race shape crowds the rear so he will likely end up racing closer than ideal — his best efforts at 7f on good suggest he is not without chance if he can find a clear passage.|

runners_data.name: Horace Wallace
runners_data.note: The third confirmed front-runner, 49 days off the track for the Fahey yard and previously beaten favourite on his win over 6f on standard; drops to OR 66 which is low, but his jumping-off point alongside Napolian and Comprador means he faces a gruelling pace battle rather than a controlled front-running opportunity.|

races.paceDynamic: Napolian, Comprador, and Horace Wallace are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a genuinely contested early gallop over Haydock's flat 7f — there will be no gift-wrapped lead for any single horse, and the trio will drag each other along at a pace that tests stamina from the opening furlong. This strong fractions scenario historically compresses the lead advantage and brings hold-up horses into the picture late, but only those capable of sustaining a finishing effort on good ground over this trip — Flyta, Norcross Brow, Galba, and Norfolk Blue all profile as potential beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Crafty Blue and Norfolk Blue are genuine closers but are shown in midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally given the number of horses seeking the same ground — Napolian and Comprador are the likeliest pair to actually boss the early sections. The race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently just off the hot pace or produce a strong sustained finish from midfield, as burn-out from the pace duel will be real by the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace duel burns leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian, Comprador, and Horace Wallace fight for position and collectively set a strong, unrelenting gallop that drains them in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The three leaders cut each other's throats through the first half, leaving the race wide open for those who have tracked the pace without over-committing — a classic hot-pace collapse at Haydock's flat 7f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses settles just behind the lead trio and times a run to pick up the pieces from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Black Endeavour or Berlinetta, racing off a strong gallop in a handy position, avoids the early battle and produces a clean run through the line — this trip suits horses who can travel comfortably and quicken once the pace collapse hits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace, while brisk, is not suicidal and one of the three leaders — most likely Napolian — gets a soft enough break to dictate without being fully challenged through every furlong.
scenarios.body: Napolian, the most progressive of the three leaders with a win over further on good ground in his recent form, could find the others blowing up while he finds an extra gear entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme and true hold-up horses thread through a tiring field in the final 100 yards — but this shape is undermined by the redistribution of Crafty Blue and Norfolk Blue.
scenarios.body: Both redistributed closers are unlikely to secure their natural deep position, reducing the probability of a late-swooping finish; Galba represents the most credible pure hold-up runner in the field and would need everything to fall perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Napolian, Comprador, and Horace Wallace will clash for the lead immediately — watch for a fierce duel in the first two furlongs that could fatally compromise all three of their finishing efforts.

Crafty Blue and Norfolk Blue are true hold-up horses running from a mid-pack position they will not naturally secure — if either becomes unbalanced or loses rhythm early while fighting for ground, their chance is essentially gone before the halfway mark.

Norcross Brow's last two wins came at 8f on good ground; while Liam Wright's claim is attractive, watch whether the drop to 7f and the strong early gallop allows him enough time to wind up his finish — he will need to be travelling well by the 3f pole.

Black Endeavour's tongue tie is applied for the first time — watch the paddock and early racing behaviour as this equipment change can settle or unsettle a horse and will determine how comfortably Shoemark can position him in the prominent spot.

Berlinetta steps back from 8f to 7f having won over the longer trip last time — watch whether the return to a shorter distance causes George Bass to be more aggressive early, potentially taking the horse out of his natural comfort zone against three committed front-runners.

races.name: Betway Capital City Handicap Stakes (London Mile Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Cosi Bello
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride for Charlie Fellowes (1 winner from 11 in 14 days, modest strike rate) and this prominent racer has solid Good-going form (5/7, one win, two placed) but steps up slightly from his recent 7f campaign — the 1m trip should suit and a top-four mark of 96 keeps him competitive.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Won on Good going at 8f last time out (form reads 900001) and returns quickly on seven days' rest for Richard Hannon — a hold-up horse who has found traffic frustrating in the past, but this honest gallop from two front-runners gives him a genuine target to aim at off the pace.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's six-year-old has consistent Good-going form but has been winless at this trip in recent starts, and his best figures have come over 7f; the hg:t (tongue-tie) is a consistent accessory, but he is likely to be shuffled back from a congested prominent group.

runners_data.name: Star Anthem
runners_data.note: Clive Cox sends this four-year-old back after a 91-day break, and his recent form at 7f-8f on softer ground hasn't been striking — his two best efforts came on Good going at 7f, but 14 days' trainer strike rate of 1/21 suggests the yard is not at its sharpest right now.

runners_data.name: Mountain Cat
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's lightly-raced three-year-old (hood, three runs only) has won at 8f on both Good and Standard going and takes a step forward into handicap company — his unexposed profile over a flat 1m track with genuine pace ahead is a compelling unknown, though the wide weight pull against elders is a leveller.

runners_data.name: Skipper
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes the ride on this five-year-old who has won at 8f on Good and Standard, but 75 days off and a trainer with 2/19 in the past fortnight raises a fitness question; he wears blinkers and has the profile to track pace, but this competitive field at OR 89 may expose him before the line.

runners_data.name: Arctic Thunder
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old won on Good going at 8f on his penultimate start and trainer has a strong 11/40 in the last 14 days — a genuine hold-up horse with Good-going form and an effective closing run, he is the trainer's best-placed runner in terms of current form and this race shape suits his style.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant booking for William Knight's four-year-old, who wears a hood and was placed twice at 8f on Good — his finishing position (8th last time) is forgettable but that was on Good going at 8f, the same conditions here, and Murphy's presence suggests the stable feels there is more to come.

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who won at 7f Good earlier this season but has been mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is already accounted for; his style_fit score of 0.92 reflects that he is unlikely to settle as far back as he needs to, and his chance is contingent on running his race from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Lost Signal
runners_data.note: Sean Levey rides this three-year-old front-runner who has a flawless 5/5 record on Good going (two wins, four placings across all five) — the joint pace-setter alongside Inspired, he will have to fight for the early lead in a contested field, and whether he can sustain his effort over 1m against older rivals is the key question.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's four-year-old has a moderate recent form string (5090-0) and his best Good-going efforts came at 8f earlier in his career — a prominent runner who is likely to get lost in the early traffic with so many rivals wanting the same position at OR 82.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's four-year-old is the second confirmed front-runner and arrives in good form (644521, won last time), but his Going record at 8f on Good is only 5/10 — if he is outpaced early by Lost Signal and burns energy chasing the leader, his stamina will be tested before the final two furlongs.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old (blinkers) is a true hold-up horse placed in four of his last five starts who has been redistributed into a midfield map position because the rear slots are overpopulated; his style_fit of 0.93 means he will likely race further forward than ideal, diluting a consistent recent form profile that includes wins at 8f-10f on Good.

runners_data.name: Triple Double A
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old (tongue-tie, hood) is ridden by the 5lb claimer Harry Vigors and has progressive form at 7f-8f on Good (three wins from seven on similar going), but recent runs over 10f-11f suggest the trainer was testing his stamina; dropping back to 1m for this flat Haydock contest may suit if he has retained his sharp end.

races.paceDynamic: Lost Signal and Inspired are the two confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field, and with six horses in total wanting prominent or lead positions — including Yorkshire, Cosi Bello, Mountain Cat, Skipper, and King Casper — the early stages will be genuinely contested rather than a solo procession. The two pacesetters will have to work to hold their berths through the first two furlongs, creating an honest, pressure-filled gallop that should stretch out the field and expose those who expend too much energy early. With congestion expected two-to-three out as prominent types attempt to improve, the race will likely develop into a thorough test of stamina-plus-speed, suiting horses that can sit just off the frenzied battle and deliver a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than those who have to sprint from cold. This race shape squarely favours the organised hold-up and well-positioned midfield horses who are tracking genuine pace — Witch Hunter, Arctic Thunder, and Tilted Kilt all profile here — rather than the true hold-up types like Leadman and Financer, who have been redistributed on the map because the field holds more genuine closers than can all get to the rear; in practice, the prominent slots are already oversubscribed, and those two are most likely to end up settling in midfield at best rather than their natural position last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lost Signal and Inspired push each other through the early stages, burning off the prominent brigade before the home turn.
scenarios.body: An honest, pressure-filled gallop set by the two front-runners drains the prominent horses, leaving the well-positioned hold-up types with a clear target turning in; horses who have settled just behind the melee hit the rising ground with reserves intact and sweep past the tiring leaders. This shape most directly benefits Witch Hunter (returning to winning form and Good going), Arctic Thunder (won at this trip on Good last time), and Tilted Kilt (Oisin Murphy aboard, Good-going placed form).

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survives Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners, most likely Lost Signal, controls the pace slightly more astutely and the genuine closers fail to make ground against the rail.
scenarios.body: Lost Signal has a perfect record on Good going (5/5 sim-going, two wins) and the class to dictate terms at a manageable tempo if Inspired is outpaced early or the two front-runners reach a tactical understanding through the first half-mile; a horse with enough early speed to track or sit a length off survives the finishing scramble as hold-up types find nowhere to go. Cosi Bello (prominent, Good-going record, Tom Marquand) and Mountain Cat (three-year-old lightly raced, won at 8f Good last time) are best placed to stay competitive in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Settles
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out early and the prominent group also fades, gifting a well-timed hold-up run from a horse who travels supremely through the race.
scenarios.body: In this scenario, the pace-setters tie each other up through the first half, creating a vacuum that a single horse travelling comfortably in midfield exploits by making a progressive move from three furlongs out without traffic interference. Leadman (David O'Meara, proven at 7f Good, in midfield by redistribution but a genuine closer on proper form) and Financer (placed in both of his last two starts, Tim Easterby yard in form) are the profile horses here, though both are racing out of role and the shape depends on them accessing ground they may not find.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Three-Year-Old Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Mountain Cat's lightly-raced profile and stamina reserve allow him to travel smoothly past tiring handicappers in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mountain Cat is a three-year-old rated 96 with only three runs to his name, trained by Saeed bin Suroor, wearing a hood, and has won twice at 8f on Good and Standard — this trip at a flat Haydock track with genuine pace to aim at is exactly the scenario that flatters an unexposed youngster. If prominent horses tire on the run-in, his youth and untapped stamina propel him past older, exposed handicappers who may have already found their level.

watchPoints.text: If Lost Signal and Inspired go stride-for-stride from the outset, the early burn rate rises sharply — watch whether Inspired blinks first before the halfway point, as this will set the true pace of the contest.

Prominent congestion is severe with at least six horses wanting the first three positions — Cosi Bello, Yorkshire, Mountain Cat, Skipper, and King Casper will all be crowding Lost Signal and Inspired in the opening two furlongs, creating a high risk of interference and pockets forming 2-3 out.

Leadman and Financer are genuine closers mapped into midfield through redistribution — if the pair cannot get their natural position at the rear they may become passengers in a muddled portion of the field rather than delivering their customary finishing runs.

Mountain Cat's hg:p (hood debut or return) is worth monitoring in the paddock — Saeed bin Suroor's use of headgear on a lightly-raced three-year-old in a competitive handicap sometimes signals that a performance step forward is expected from the stable.

Arctic Thunder's trainer Ed Walker has 11 winners from 40 runners in the past 14 days — a live yard with a horse whose style genuinely suits this pace shape and who won over the same trip on Good going recently; a drifting SP would be the only flag against.

races.name: Betway Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Suggy
runners_data.note: Genuinely strong on this track and trip with two wins over 8f on Standard-equivalent going, though her hold-up style means she will be last away and entirely reliant on the pace being strong enough through the early stages; Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) adds interest but her sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places on Good proper is worth flagging.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by Ross Burdon whose trainer is in poor recent form (0/3 in 14 days); last won over this trip on Standard going and has not troubled the judge on Good ground in five attempts, which is a material concern when his role here is to burn energy fighting for the early lead.

runners_data.name: Phantom Watch
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer has a healthy recent strike rate and this 3yo has won on Good ground over this exact trip, making him one of the classiest profile fits in the field; wears a visor suggesting he needs mental engagement, and his hold-up-to-midfield style should find him in a good position if the two pace-setters do the expected donkey work.

runners_data.name: Home Hero
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an aggressive freshness concern, and although he won over 8f on Good ground in his last campaign, his record over longer trips on Good is poor (5th, 9th, 8th); the front-running role here demands a ready horse, and the quick reappearance alongside a trainer running multiple in the race adds risk.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's apprentice-ridden 3yo arrives in excellent recent form — placed five times from nine runs on Good and won over 7f on Good, stepping back up to a mile where she has finished second twice at Haydock on this exact going; Conor Whiteley's 3lb claim is a legitimate edge and her prominent style is the tactical sweet spot in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Forever Endless
runners_data.note: Three runs in, all finishing fifth, including twice at Haydock on Good — a hold-up type by nature who will struggle to get to the rear in a field with several rivals displaced from their preferred positions; the redistribution note here is genuine, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 underlines that finishing this race from her natural closing berth is unlikely.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Standard, which is an eye-catching form uptick, but has a poor sim-going record on Good proper (0W0P from 12 runs) and is a natural closer who carries a STYLE_FIT caveat — her finishing kick depends on being further back than this race shape will allow, which tempers confidence despite the recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: Carries the lowest OR in the field at 54 and has a consistent finishing record of midfield-to-rear placings across seven similar assignments; flagged for fading in the finish and her redistribution out of a true hold-up role compounds the concern — Matthew Lloyd Slater's 5lb claim helps the weight, but this profile looks stretched in all plausible race shapes here.

races.paceDynamic: Director's Cut and Home Hero are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner field, and with both likely to push for the early lead at Haydock's flat mile, an honest, pressured gallop is the most probable outcome — neither looks the type to simply concede the front without a fight. That sustained pace through the middle stages sets up a race that should play into the hands of horses who can settle just off the leaders and pick up through the final two furlongs, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the most favoured tactical position. Sandy Craic, who has strong course and distance form on Good ground, is ideally placed to stalk the pace from a handy position, while Phantom Watch has the profile to travel through from a touch deeper. The field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Forever Endless, Sunshine And Roses, and Golden Mabel are all natural closers but will likely find themselves racing closer than ideal given the competitive pace dynamic, meaning their true finishing kicks may be compromised; Director's Cut and Home Hero are the most likely to actually secure the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Director's Cut and Home Hero fight for the lead and set a genuine honest gallop, the race falls apart for the front two in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The pressured early fractions will leave both pace-setters vulnerable in the final furlong, handing the advantage to a horse who has tracked them closely throughout; Sandy Craic's consistent form at Haydock on Good ground makes this profile ideal. Phantom Watch, with three wins or placings from four outings on Good, also fits this shape perfectly from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Home Hero or Director's Cut establishes a clear, unchallenged lead early and the other drops away, the pace becomes more controlled and the front-runner conserves enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: A measured, uncontested gallop would allow the leader to dictate fractions through the middle mile and keep enough in reserve to repel challengers; Home Hero has a win from eight starts on Good ground and the experience to exploit a soft lead. Sandy Craic's prominent style means she would still be dangerous, but a lone front-runner setting a comfortable tempo suits horses who can see the race out from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn out quickly and the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, creating a true end-to-end test that sets up a late run.
scenarios.body: Suggy has the strongest hold-up credentials in the field with a genuine late-finishing profile and two wins over this course-and-distance on Standard-equivalent going, giving her the best realistic chance from the rear. Phantom Watch also has the class and Good-ground form to close powerfully if the pace has genuinely been strong enough, though the redistributed trio of Forever Endless, Sunshine And Roses, and Golden Mabel are less likely to be in their natural position to fully capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the early lead battle causes interference or a chaotic early order that bunches the field, disrupting rhythm for the front-runners and pushing closers further back than intended.
scenarios.body: A disorganised race shape at Haydock's flat mile tends to compress the field through the middle stages, rewarding horses with tactical versatility who can find a clean run; Sandy Craic's consistent placing record and adaptability makes her the likeliest beneficiary. Phantom Watch's visor headgear suggests a horse who needs things to fall right, and a scrambled mid-race could serve her well if she gets a clean passage.

watchPoints.text: Director's Cut and Home Hero are on a collision course for the early lead — watch which one blinks first out of the stalls, as the one who concedes the front may drop dramatically back through the field and compromise any each-way hope.

Home Hero ran just two days ago; watch for any signs of a flat, below-par display in the early exchanges that would suggest the quick turnaround has left him short, which would fundamentally change the pace dynamic if he fails to press forward.

Sandy Craic's jockey Conor Whiteley takes a 3lb claim but is apprentice-grade — watch whether she gets a clean, unhurried passage in the first two furlongs, as being blocked in a tight eight-runner field early could negate her strong positional profile.

Phantom Watch's visor is a flag for a horse who can switch off mentally mid-race; watch whether Liam Wright keeps him covered up early or asks him to travel prominently, as the headgear implies he needs to be kept interested rather than allowed to idle.

Suggy has the best course-and-distance record in the field but her sim-going data shows 0 wins and 0 places from 9 runs on Good — watch for whether the ground reading throughout the day firms up at all, which could materially shift her prospects given her form base on Standard-equivalent surfaces.
